source_text: Verum videamus et reliqua. Peccatum autem non deputabatur, ait Apostolus, cum lex non esset [n112] ; post quod tu subdis: Erat ergo, sed non deputabatur, sicut alibi dicit: " Per legem cognitio peccati " [n113] . Si ergo per legem peccati est facta cognitio et peccatum traducis ante legem non imputabatur, ostende hoc imputatum fuisse sub lege. Nam si per legem peccati cognitio, ante legem ignoratio peccati, ambigi non potest hanc fuisse causam maximam promulgandae legis, ut proderetur et caveretur, quod prius latebat.
pass_a_gloss: But let us see also the remaining things. But sin was not reckoned, says the Apostle, when the law was not; after which you subjoin: It was therefore, but was not reckoned, as he says elsewhere: 'Through the law is the knowledge of sin.' If therefore through the law knowledge of sin was made and the sin of the tradux was not imputed before the law, show that this was imputed under the law. For if through the law knowledge of sin, before the law ignorance of sin, it cannot be doubted that this was the greatest cause of promulgating the law, that that might be betrayed and guarded against which previously lay hidden.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Let us also examine what follows. ‘But sin was not reckoned,’ the apostle says, ‘when there was no law’ (Romans 5:13). You then add: ‘It therefore existed but was not reckoned, as he says elsewhere: “Through the law comes knowledge of sin”’ (Romans 3:20; Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.46). If, then, knowledge of sin came through the law, and the sin of inherited transmission was not imputed before the law, show that it was imputed under the law. If through the law came knowledge of sin, and before the law there was ignorance of sin, there can be no doubt that a chief reason for promulgating the law was to expose, and enable people to avoid, what had previously been hidden.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
